questions.q: What are the primary dietary sources and main functions of carbohydrates in the human body?
a: Sources: bread, rice, pasta; Function: primary source of quick chemical energy for respiration
Sources: meat, fish, eggs; Function: long-term thermal insulation

Sources: vegetable oils, butter; Function: building cell membranes

questions.q: Which nutrient group is essential for growth, tissue repair, and the formation of enzymes and antibodies?
What are the main functions of lipids (fats and oils) in a balanced human diet?

questions.q: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting, and what deficiency results if it is lacking?
a: Vitamin K; prolonged bleeding times due to poor clot formation

questions.q: What deficiency disease is caused by a lack of Vitamin C in the diet?
a: Scurvy (characterized by bleeding gums and poor wound healing)

questions.q: Which mineral is a crucial component of hemoglobin in red blood cells, and what condition results from its deficiency?
a: Iron; iron-deficiency anemia resulting in fatigue and poor oxygen transport

questions.q: Why is dietary fiber (roughage) an important component of a healthy human diet even though it cannot be digested?

It adds bulk to food, stimulating peristalsis and preventing constipation

questions.q: What is a balanced diet defined as?
a: Eating only raw vegetables and fruit every day
Consuming maximum calories regardless of activity
Consuming equal quantities of all chemical elements
A diet containing all the necessary nutrients in correct proportions and amounts to provide energy and maintain health

questions.q: What is the primary function of Vitamin D in the human body, and what deficiency disease does it cause?
a: Function: assisting calcium and phosphorus absorption for strong bones and teeth; Disease: rickets

questions.q: Why is water vital as a component of the human diet?
a: It acts as a solid skeletal support
It is converted directly into protein
It acts as a solvent for metabolic reactions, transport medium, and cooling agent

questions.q: What is coronary heart disease (CHD) often linked to in terms of diet?

Consuming high amounts of Vitamin C

questions.q: Which of the following defines malnutrition?

Eating exactly the correct number of calories

questions.q: What is the main role of dietary fiber in the human digestive tract?

questions.q: Which of the following foods is richest in dietary fiber (roughage)?
a: Whole grain bread, beans, and fresh vegetables

a: Increased likelihood of type 2 diabetes, joint strain, and cardiovascular problems in later life

questions.q: What is the primary dietary source of Vitamin C?

a: Breaking down large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed

questions.q: Which of the following is a reliable plant-based source of complete or complementary proteins for vegetarians?

a: Vitamin C — tissue repair and immune function
